Halan Hollwood first lived in Gulton with his wife Nynelle Stenworth. He then followed her to Coldcombe (Chapter 18), where their son Ilrald was born. In Chapter 36 he rode out of Coldcombe and by the next market day was living in Gulton. Nynelle went to live in Gulton as well. No later paragraph moves him again.

Answer: Gulton

Rira Stenworth's latest recorded move: Chapter 34, "Rira Stenworth packed a single trunk and moved from Harrowgate to Yarlton." Later entries about her (Chapter 39, mending a sleeve; sorting letters) don't mention another move.

Answer: Yarlton

Tassa Brackwood married Colan Lindson and lived in Bryngate (Ch. 13). In Ch. 22 she left Bryngate and settled in Yarlton. Later mentions of Tassa (Ch. 39: mending a sleeve; talked of going to Mirecombe but stayed where she was) give no new move. So the latest residence is Yarlton.

Answer: Yarlton

Nynelle Hollmere's later moves: in Chapter 14 she found work in Miremere and moved there, not returning to Salwick. In Chapter 23, she married Elnar Brackwood at Fenmere, and the couple lived in Fenmere from then on. In Chapter 33 their son Nydan Brackwood was born, and the family lived in Fenmere.

The latest information places her in Fenmere.

Answer: Fenmere

Thidrek Corrett moved from Dunwick to Fenmere (Chapter 23), and Jolia Hollett followed him there. A rumor in Chapter 32 said he had drowned, but the Epilogue shows him alive and well at the summer fair in Fenmere. The rumor is therefore false, and the latest known residence is Fenmere.

Answer: Fenmere

Tracing Daena Wexwood's moves:
- Ch 25: moved from Quenwick to Staveton.
- Ch 35: after a quarrel, quit Staveton for Dunholt.
- Ch 37: after a quarrel, quit Dunholt for Miremere.
- Ch 39: wed Zanar Hollwood at Miremere; the couple lived in Miremere from then on.

The latest information places her in Miremere.

Answer: Miremere

Colan Lindson lived in Bryngate, where he wed Tassa Brackwood. In Chapter 22 the record says "Colan Lindson followed her to Yarlton within the month." It doesn't say who "her" is, but it is the latest move recorded for him, and no later passage moves him again.

Answer: Yarlton

Madan Brackwood first lived in Mirecombe with his wife Wevie Lindner. The latest relevant move is in Chapter 27: "Madan Brackwood followed her to Salmere within the month." The text doesn't say who "her" is. Chapter 22 has a rumor that he drowned, but that is gossip, and he appears alive in Chapter 35. No later passage moves him again, so Salmere is his last known home.

Answer: Salmere

The most recent move I can trace is Chapter 39, where Jotho Corrett "went along to live in Mirecombe as well." The paragraph naming who moved first is missing from the excerpts, so the following lines about Cobin and Ilrine suggest, but do not confirm, that Cobin was the one who moved there.

Earlier, Cobin followed his wife from Quenwick to Yarlton (Chapter 6). Nothing after that places him anywhere else.

Answer: Mirecombe

Nyrine Wexwood married Daric Brackwood at Mirecombe in Chapter 25, and the couple lived in Mirecombe from then on. The later chapters record no move for her.

Answer: Mirecombe

Jovus Brackwood rode out of Fenmere and by the next market day was living in Harrowgate (Ch. 6). He married Rira Stenworth at Harrowgate and the couple lived there from then on (Ch. 7). Their daughter Neena was born in Harrowgate (Ch. 30), and later passages place him in Harrowgate (Ch. 32). In Ch. 34, "Red Jovus followed her to Yarlton within the month." This is a move, but "her" is unspecified. Tassa Brackwood settled in Yarlton in Ch. 22. Yet Ch. 33 (before Ch. 34) has Red Jovus giving the bone chalice to the wife of Jovus Brackwood, which is odd, though it doesn't change the residence. "Red Jovus" is Jovus Brackwood's nickname, so the Ch. 34 line means he moved to Yarlton, and no later passage moves him again.

The "her" is probably Rira (his wife) or Tassa. Either way, Jovus went to Yarlton. Later lines (Ch. 37, 39) mention Neena and Brenelle in Harrowgate, but not Jovus himself.

Answer: Yarlton

Cotho Hollwood left Wilhaven for Coldcombe after a quarrel (Chapter 2). In Chapter 33 he married Gamira Brackwood at Coldcombe, and the couple "lived in Coldcombe from then on." Nothing later records another move. The Chapter 40 rumor that he secretly wed Jolia Hollett is only gossip, so it doesn't change this.

Answer: Coldcombe

Eldette Corrett married Halan Hollett at Dunholt in Chapter 31, and the couple lived there from then on. In Chapter 37 their son Jozek Hollett was born, and the family still lived in Dunholt. The record shows no later move for her.

Answer: Dunholt

Aessa Hollwood left Wilhaven and settled in Salford (Chapter 13). Later, in Chapter 26, she married Ellan Lindner in the chapel at Salford, and the couple lived in Salford from then on. No later chapter mentions her moving elsewhere.

Answer: Salford

Nynelle Stenworth moved from Gulton to Coldcombe in Chapter 18 and did not return. In Chapter 22 her son Ilrald was born and the family lived in Coldcombe. Chapter 24 still places her in the hill farms of Coldcombe. Islan Lindner died at Staveton in Chapter 26. Her next recorded move, back to Gulton, comes only in Chapter 36, so she was still in Coldcombe when he died.

Answer: Coldcombe

Cotho Hollwood quit Wilhaven after a quarrel in Chapter 2 and took lodgings in Coldcombe. Mazek Hollwood died of the coughing sickness in Chapter 10, and no move by Cotho is recorded between those two points. The Chapter 5 report that Cotho and Thiena had wed in secret is only gossip, and the Chapter 9 line about Thiena following "him" to Salford does not name Cotho.

Answer: Coldcombe

Islis Lindson belonged to the Lindson household in the market town of Bryngate (Chapter 1). Senelle Brackwood died in Chapter 5, after a fall from the mill loft. Nothing before that point says Islis moved away from Bryngate. Chapter 2 also shows the Lindsons still in Bryngate.

Answer: Bryngate

Brevie Hollmere died in Chapter 9 (¶2442). The latest earlier record of Thidrek Corrett's residence is in Chapters 1 and 3. He was married to Jolia Hollett, and the family lived in Mirecombe. His moves to Dunwick and then Fenmere come later, in Chapters 18 and 23, so they don't apply at the time of her death.

Answer: Mirecombe

Eldette Corrett was the eldest child of Cobin and Ilrine Corrett, who lived in the river crossing at Quenwick. Nyvie Hollett died in Chapter 6, a little after Ilrine left for Yarlton and Cobin followed her there. Nothing in the record says Eldette left Quenwick. Later Quenwick scenes, such as the ribbon at the stall, also place her there.

Answer: Quenwick

Seena Hollett was part of the Hollett household in Mirecombe, and the record never shows her moving away. Orrine Stenworth died in Chapter 22 (kicked by a cart horse at Coldcombe). Just after that, Seena is still in Mirecombe, talking with Madan Brackwood in the hill farms there.

Answer: Mirecombe

Cotho Hollwood left Wilhaven for good after a quarrel in Chapter 2 and took lodgings in Coldcombe. No later move for him appears before Seena Orlwood drowned in the Mirecombe flood in Chapter 11. In Chapter 9, "Thiena Hollwood followed him to Salford," but the excerpt doesn't say who "him" is, so I did not count it as a move by Cotho.

Answer: Coldcombe

Islis Lindson was the wife of Colan Lindson, and the record says the coughing sickness took her one summer and she was buried at Bryngate (Chapter 9). The latest earlier information on Rira Stenworth is from Chapter 7, where she married Red Jovus at Harrowgate and the couple lived there from then on. Her move from Harrowgate to Yarlton comes only in Chapter 34, long after Islis died.

Answer: Harrowgate

Conar Hollett's household lived in the hill farms of Mirecombe from the start. His wife Nyvie was buried at Mirecombe in Chapter 6. Later passages place him there again, in Chapter 26 and the Epilogue. Nothing in the record shows him moving away before Ridan Corrett died at Gulton in Chapter 20.

Answer: Mirecombe

Ilzek Wexwood died in Chapter 29 (buried at Staveton, dead of a long wasting sickness).

Orvie Hollett's residence by then: she was born at Wilhaven, and in Chapter 16 she married Rozek Hollwood at Mirecombe and the couple lived in Mirecombe from then on. Later paragraphs (Chapters 22 and 28) have their daughters born there, with the family living in Mirecombe. Nothing records a move afterward.

Answer: Mirecombe

Dadette Lindner died at Staveton in Chapter 15. Nynelle Stenworth and her husband Halan Hollwood were living in Gulton at that point. Their son Isbin was born there in Chapter 10, and their son Zanar was born there in Chapter 16, just after the death. She only moved to Coldcombe later, in Chapter 18.

Answer: Gulton

Orbin Stenworth was originally married to Orrine Stenworth. Orrine died of a kick from a cart horse at Coldcombe (Chapter 22). Later, in Chapter 26, Nylis Corrett and Orbin Stenworth were wed at Mirecombe. Chapter 33 shows them with a son, Garald, in Staveton, and Chapter 38 adds a daughter, Rolde. Nothing later says Nylis died or that they separated.

Answer: Nylis Corrett

Thiena Hollwood first married Ridan Corrett, and they lived in Quenwick. In Chapter 21 she married Maric Lindson at Gulton. Maric later moved to Coldcombe, and she followed him there. They had a daughter, Elnelle Lindson, in Chapter 33. Nothing later records Maric's death or a separation, so Maric Lindson is her latest spouse.

Answer: Maric Lindson

Lutho Hollmere's first wife, Brevie Hollmere, died in Chapter 9. In Chapter 38, Thivie Brackwood took Lutho in marriage at Dunholt, and nothing later records her death or a further marriage for Lutho.

Answer: Thivie Brackwood

Conar Hollett's wife was Nyvie Hollett. A long sickness took her in Chapter 6 and she was buried at Mirecombe. Nothing in the record shows Conar marrying again. The report in Chapter 38 that he had drowned was only a rumor, and the Epilogue shows him alive at the Mirecombe fair, so he has no living spouse.

Answer: none

Aessa Hollwood was introduced in Chapter 1 as the wife of Mazek Hollwood. In Chapter 26 she married Ellan Lindner at the chapel in Salford, and the couple lived in Salford from then on. Nothing later says Ellan Lindner died or that they parted. Chapter 32 has Aessa talking with Ellan, and Chapter 40 mentions Ellan Lindner. Neither suggests a change.

Mazek's earlier marriage to Aessa also doesn't conflict with this, since the Salford wedding is the latest marital event recorded for her.

Answer: Ellan Lindner

Maric Lindson was first married to Seena Orlwood (Chapter 1). In Chapter 21 he married Thiena Hollwood at Gulton, and in Chapter 33 they had a daughter, Elnelle Lindson. In Chapter 35 Thiena moved to Gulton and Maric went along. In Chapter 38 he is still speaking with her. The plague story in Chapter 17 was only a rumor, and nothing in the record says either spouse died or that they separated.

Answer: Thiena Hollwood

Colan Lindson's first wife, Islis, died of the coughing sickness in Chapter 9. In Chapter 13 he married Tassa Brackwood at Bryngate, and in Chapter 16 she bore his daughter Rorine. Nothing later records Tassa's death or a further marriage for Colan.

Answer: Tassa Brackwood

Elnar Brackwood was first married to Senelle Brackwood. In Chapter 5, Senelle died after a fall from the mill loft and was buried at Fenmere. In Chapter 23, Elnar took Nynelle Hollmere in marriage at Fenmere, and the couple lived there from then on. Chapter 33 records a son, Nydan Brackwood, born to Nynelle Hollmere and Elnar. Nothing later says Nynelle died or that Elnar remarried.

Answer: Nynelle Hollmere

Nynelle Stenworth and Halan Hollwood were husband and wife (Chapter 1), and nothing later ends the marriage. They went on to have several children, and later in the record Nynelle follows Halan when he moves to Gulton. A report that she had drowned appears only as an inn rumor, so it is not a fact. The Nynelle Hollmere who married Elnar Brackwood is a different person.

Answer: Halan Hollwood

Halan Hollwood is married to Nynelle Stenworth (Chapter 1 ¶279). Later chapters keep them together as husband and wife in Gulton, with children Rozek, Isbin, Zanar and Ilrald. Nothing in the record says Nynelle died or that they separated. Chapter 18's "Halan Hollwood followed her to Coldcombe" does not change this. The later reference to "the wife of Halan Hollwood" is consistent with it.

Answer: Nynelle Stenworth

The record says that in Chapter 26, in the chapel at Salford, Aessa Hollwood married Ellan Lindner, and the couple lived in Salford from then on. Nothing later in the record mentions the marriage ending or Aessa Hollwood dying. Chapter 32 has Aessa speaking with Ellan, which fits them still being together.

Answer: Aessa Hollwood

Rorine Lindson's marriage appears in Chapter 38: "Before the autumn was out, Ilrald Hollwood took Rorine Lindson in marriage at Coldcombe. The couple lived in Coldcombe from then on."

Nothing later in the record says Ilrald Hollwood died or that the marriage ended. Chapters 39 and 40 still mention Rorine, but only in connection with promises, not a change of spouse.

Answer: Ilrald Hollwood

Rira Stenworth married Red Jovus (Jovus Brackwood) at Harrowgate in Chapter 7. In Chapter 30 she had a daughter, Neena Brackwood, with Jovus Brackwood. In Chapter 34 she moved from Harrowgate to Yarlton, but no divorce or death of the spouse is recorded. Chapter 21 mentions Rira winning a bone chalice from "the husband of Rira Stenworth" at cards, which is consistent with the marriage still standing. Chapter 2 has gossip about Thidrek Corrett, which is only a rumor.

Answer: Jovus Brackwood

Rozek Hollwood married Orvie Hollett at Mirecombe (Chapter 16), and they had children Hamira and Rimira. No later paragraph reports Orvie's death or a separation. Gossip about other people's secret weddings doesn't affect this.

Answer: Orvie Hollett

Ortho Corrett is the son of Ridan Corrett and Thiena Hollwood. In Chapter 29, Movie Lindson married Ortho Corrett in the chapel at Bryngate, and the couple lived in Bryngate from then on. In Chapter 36, Movie Lindson gave birth to Karic Corrett, with Ortho Corrett as the father. Nothing later records Movie's death or a separation.

Answer: Movie Lindson

Orvie Hollett and Rozek Hollwood were wed at Mirecombe (Chapter 16) and had daughters Hamira and Rimira, who lived in Mirecombe. Nothing in the record says Rozek died or that they separated. A Chapter 40 rumor about Jolia Hollett marrying Cotho Hollwood doesn't concern Orvie. So the latest information still has Orvie married to Rozek Hollwood.

Answer: Rozek Hollwood

Chapter 38 ¶6286 says "Before the autumn was out, Thivie Brackwood took Lutho in marriage at Dunholt. The couple lived in Dunholt from then on." This is the only marriage recorded for Thivie, and nothing later says it ended. The name "Lutho" has no surname given in the record. The only Lutho named elsewhere is Lutho Hollmere (Chapter 1), who is already married to Brevie Hollmere and is presumably the father of Fetho and Nynelle. A different Lutho could be meant, but the record names no other, so the spouse is given as Lutho, with Lutho Hollmere as the only candidate surname.

Answer: Lutho

Cobin Corrett's wife is Ilrine Corrett, as recorded in Chapter 1. Later she left Quenwick for Yarlton and he followed her there. Nothing in the record shows a divorce, a death or a new marriage, and Ilrine is still active in Chapter 39.

Answer: Ilrine Corrett

Chapter 25 records that Daric Brackwood took Nyrine Wexwood in marriage at Mirecombe, and the couple lived there from then on. Later in the record, Daric Brackwood still appears alive: in Chapter 27 he agrees with Nyrine's remark about the price of salt. No later passage mentions a death or a new spouse for Nyrine. The Chapter 39 wedding at Miremere is Daena Wexwood's, not Nyrine's.

Answer: Daric Brackwood

Chapter 26 ¶4703 records "Islan died of the coughing sickness at Staveton," and ¶4716 shows his belongings being handed on to Wevie Lindner. Nothing later in the record contradicts this.

Answer: no

The record states in Chapter 11 that "Seena Orlwood died of drowning in the flood at Mirecombe." Later mentions of "Seena" without a surname appear to refer to Seena Hollett, and nothing says Seena Orlwood came back to life, so she is not alive at the end.

Answer: no

In Chapter 26, the record says that old age took Isbin Hollwood in his sleep that autumn, and he was buried at Gulton. Later chapters still show an "Isbin" in some lines, but those fall before Chapter 26, and no later passage says he was alive again. The latest information is therefore that he died.

Answer: no

Chapter 35 says "That winter, old age, quietly in sleep took Wevie Lindner; she was buried at Salmere." That is the latest information about her state, and it is a death. Later chapters (36–40) show nothing that contradicts it, and the mentions of Wevie in earlier chapters are earlier events.

Answer: no

Chapter 15 ¶3200 records that Dadette Lindner died of a fall from the mill loft at Staveton. The later material contains nothing that says otherwise.

Answer: no

Chapter 5 states: "That summer, a fall from the mill loft took Senelle Brackwood; she was buried at Fenmere." This is a death. Later, Chapter 27 says "Madan Brackwood followed her to Salmere within the month," but that refers to a different person. No later info indicates Senelle returned to life.

Answer: no

Chapter 9 records that Brevie Hollmere died that summer in her sleep of old age and was buried at Salwick. Nothing later in the record says otherwise.

Answer: no

Islis Lindson was the wife of Colan Lindson (Chapter 1). In Chapter 9, "the coughing sickness took the wife of Colan Lindson; she was buried at Bryngate." Colan later married Tassa Brackwood in Chapter 13, which confirms Islis was no longer living. Nothing later in the record shows her alive.

Answer: no

Chapter 20 ¶3787 records that Ridan Corrett died of old age, quietly in sleep at Gulton. Nothing later in the record contradicts this.

Answer: no

Chapter 10 records that the coughing sickness took Mazek that autumn and that he was buried at Wilhaven. Nothing later says otherwise, so he is not alive at the end of the record.

Answer: no

In Chapter 6, a long wasting sickness took Nyvie Hollett, and she was buried at Mirecombe. Nothing later in the record contradicts this, so she is dead by the end.

Answer: no

In Chapter 22, ¶4167, the record says Orrine Stenworth died of a kick from a cart horse at Coldcombe. Nothing later says she is alive again. Later mentions of "Orrine" appear in Chapter 12, 14 and 17, all before her death. No later passage revives her.

Answer: no

The record contains a rumor that Maric Lindson died of plague, started by Orrine from a peddler. Rumors are not facts. There are later events showing Maric alive: he married Thiena Hollwood, had a daughter, Elnelle, in Coldcombe, and later lived in Gulton. Maric is mentioned as alive in later chapters, such as chapter 35 ("Maric Lindson went along to live in Gulton as well"). No death is confirmed.

Answer: yes

Madan Brackwood is alive. The Chapter 22 report that he drowned crossing the estuary was only an inn rumor, with no body seen. The Chapter 27 line "followed her to Salmere within the month" describes a move, not a death, since deaths in this record are stated outright (as with Senelle's burial). In Chapter 35 Madan is still active, and he receives the glass comb that had belonged to Wevie Lindner.

Answer: yes

The record has a rumor in Chapter 32 that Thidrek Corrett drowned crossing the estuary, though no body was ever seen. That is gossip, not fact. The Epilogue then says he was seen hale and well at the summer fair in Fenmere, so he is alive at the end.

Answer: yes

The only hint of her death is Ortho's claim in Chapter 34 that Nynelle Stenworth drowned crossing the estuary. That is an unconfirmed report, since "no body was ever seen". Chapter 36 later says she went along to live in Gulton, so she is alive after that claim, and nothing afterward says she died.

Answer: yes

Daena Wexwood's death is reported only as a rumor in Chapter 34 (started by Fedette, who had it from a peddler), so it is not a fact. Later she is still active: in Chapter 39 she argues, counts coins, and marries Zanar Hollwood at Miremere. Nothing afterward records her death. Ilzek's death is the one that is confirmed (Chapter 29).

Answer: yes

The only claim of Conar Hollett's death is a rumor: Halan Hollett told people at the inn that Conar had drowned crossing the estuary, though no body was ever seen. The epilogue then states that Conar was seen hale and well at the summer fair in Mirecombe, which is the latest information and contradicts the rumor.

Answer: yes

The record shows no death for Elnar Brackwood. Senelle Brackwood died in Chapter 5, and Madan was rumored drowned, but nothing says Elnar died. His latest appearances are in Chapter 33, where he has a son, Nydan, with Nynelle Hollmere and talks with him in Fenmere.

Answer: yes

Halan Hollwood appears in many scenes through the late chapters (e.g., Chapter 36 he rode out of Coldcombe and settled in Gulton). The only death noted is Isbin Hollwood in Chapter 26. No record of Halan Hollwood dying.

Answer: yes

Pebin Wexwood's latest appearances are in Chapter 37, where he left Harrowgate and settled in Bryngate. Nothing in the record reports his death. The only death rumor concerns Daena Wexwood (plague), and Ilzek Wexwood's death is stated as fact. So Pebin is alive as of the latest information.

Answer: yes

Nynelle Hollmere, daughter of Lutho and Brevie Hollmere, married Elnar Brackwood and lived in Fenmere. She had a son, Nydan Brackwood, in Chapter 33, and no later passage reports her death. The drowning rumor in Chapter 34 concerns Nynelle Stenworth, a different person.

Answer: yes

No death of Cotho Hollwood is recorded anywhere in the material. He appears alive in the latest chapters (Chapter 40), where he sends the iron chalice by carrier, buys a ribbon and takes part in conversations.

Answer: yes

Aera Corrett was born in Fenmere to Jolia Hollett and Thidrek Corrett (Chapter 23). She appears in later passages only in ordinary scenes, and nothing in the record reports her death. The only death-related items concern Thidrek Corrett, whose reported drowning was just a rumor (he was later seen hale and well), and Ridan Corrett, who died of old age.

Answer: yes

Searching the record for any death of Ellan Lindner turns up nothing. The deaths I found are Dadette Lindner (a fall from the mill loft) and Wevie Lindner (died in her sleep one winter). The most recent entry about Ellan is in Chapter 40, where he is still around, and he married Aessa Hollwood in Chapter 26.

Answer: yes

The iron chalice was tracked through its transfers in the record:

- It belonged to Nyrine Wexwood, who gave it to Eldette Corrett.
- Jotho the Younger won it from Eldette Corrett at cards.
- Jotho Corrett gave it to Halan Hollwood. I took "Jotho Corrett" to be the same person as "Jotho the Younger".
- Halan Hollwood gave it to Cotho Hollwood.
- Cotho Hollwood sent it by carrier to Ortho Corrett, who received it safely. This is the last transfer in the record.

Answer: Ortho Corrett

The pewter chalice was first kept by Ellan Lindner. In Chapter 25 it reached Fetho Hollmere by parcel from the youngest son of Dadette Lindner. In Chapter 40, Fetho Hollmere gave it to Ulvie Hollwood, and no later passage moves it again.

Answer: Ulvie Hollwood

The iron ledger passes through these hands in order:

- Senelle Brackwood owned it, then gave it to Elnar Brackwood.
- Elnar Brackwood gave it to the only son of Nyvie Hollett (Halan, who sent it on to Ridan).
- Ridan Corrett owned it next, and it went to Thiena Hollwood.
- The youngest daughter of Aessa Hollwood gave it to Cotho Brackwood.
- Cotho Brackwood gave it to the wife of Halan Hollwood.
- Nynelle Stenworth gave it to the wife of Cotho Brackwood. This is the last mention.

The record does not name Cotho Brackwood's wife.

Answer: the wife of Cotho Brackwood

The bone chalice passed through these hands in order:

- Tassa Brackwood kept it (Chapter 1).
- Tassa gave it to Red Jovus (Chapter 5).
- Rira won it at cards from the husband of Rira Stenworth (Chapter 21).
- Rira Stenworth pressed it into Red Jovus's hands (Chapter 30).
- Red Jovus gave it to the wife of Jovus Brackwood (Chapter 33).

No later passage moves it again, so the wife of Jovus Brackwood holds it at the end. The record never gives her own name.

Answer: the wife of Jovus Brackwood

The pewter comb first appears with Halan Hollwood, who kept it in a cedar box (Chapter 1). Its latest mention is in Chapter 38, where the husband of Nynelle Stenworth pressed it into her hands and took nothing for it. No later passage moves it, so Nynelle Stenworth holds it at the end.

Answer: Nynelle Stenworth

Tracing the jade mirror:
- Fedette Orlwood owned it (Ch1).
- Cotho Hollwood won it from Fedette (Ch3).
- Ilena Orlwood won it from Cotho (Ch12).
- It went from Ilena Orlwood to Cotho Hollwood (Ch17).

No later event involves the jade mirror, so Cotho Hollwood holds it at the end.

Answer: Cotho Hollwood

The garnet mirror passed through these hands in order:

- Thidrek Corrett sent it to Islis Lindson.
- Islis gave it to the youngest daughter of Colan Lindson.
- Jotho Corrett won it from Ridette Lindson at cards.
- Ridette's husband gave it to Feten Lindner.
- Eldette Corrett won it from Feten at cards.
- In Chapter 39, a parcel from Eldette Corrett reached Colan with the garnet mirror inside, "now his to keep."

The last transfer names only "Colan." The only full name given for a Colan in the record is Colan Lindson, so I take that to be him.

Answer: Colan Lindson

The only passage that says who owned the oak comb is Chapter 1 ¶1211, where it is among the possessions of Halan Hollett. Chapter 1 ¶1430 mentions the oak comb again, but only as part of a Quenwick vault law. No later passage records it being given away, sold or lost, so Halan Hollett still holds it.

Answer: Halan Hollett

The glass comb passed through these hands in order:
- Dadette Lindner owned it first.
- Seena Hollett won it from her at cards.
- Seena gave it to Madrek Orlwood.
- Fedette Orlwood won it from Madrek at cards, then sent it to Islan.
- Islan Lindner's things, including the comb, were handed to Wevie Lindner.
- In Chapter 35, the comb that Wevie Lindner had owned "went to Madan."

The record names only one Madan, Madan Brackwood (Chapter 24), so I take this to be him. The text of Chapter 35 gives just the first name.

Answer: Madan Brackwood

The jade ring: Chapter 1 says it belonged to Orvie Hollett. In Chapter 22, "A parcel from Orvie reached Halan Hollett; inside was the jade ring, now his to keep." No later information about the ring appears.

Answer: Halan Hollett

The amber mirror passed through these holders in order:

- Brevie Hollmere kept it, then it went to Lutho Hollmere.
- Fetho Hollmere won it from Lutho, then sent it to Conar Hollett.
- Isnar Brackwood won it from Conar Hollett.
- The eldest daughter of Nyvie Hollett won it from Isnar Brackwood, fairly, and kept it.

That is the last mention of the mirror. The record doesn't give her name, only that she is Nyvie Hollett's eldest daughter.

Answer: The eldest daughter of Nyvie Hollett

The only record of the jade chalice's ownership says it belonged to Islan Lindner, head of the Lindner household. It passes to the holder's eldest living child only when the holder dies, and the record never reports Islan's death or any later transfer of it. So Islan Lindner still holds it.

Answer: Islan Lindner

The iron chalice passed through these holders, in order:

1. Nyrine Wexwood owned it first.
2. Nyrine gave it to Eldette Corrett.
3. Jotho (the Younger) Corrett won it from Eldette at cards.
4. Jotho Corrett gave it to Halan Hollwood.
5. Halan Hollwood gave it to Cotho Hollwood.
6. Cotho Hollwood sent it by carrier to Ortho Corrett, who received it safely.

Ortho Corrett is the current holder, so the holder immediately before was Cotho Hollwood.

Answer: Cotho Hollwood

The pewter chalice was last passed on in Chapter 40, when Fetho Hollmere gave it to Ulvie Hollwood. No later transfer appears, so Ulvie Hollwood is the current holder. Fetho Hollmere had received it in Chapter 25, in a parcel from the youngest son of Dadette Lindner.

Answer: Fetho Hollmere

The latest transfer of the iron ledger is in Chapter 31, where Nynelle Stenworth gave it to the wife of Cotho Brackwood. That makes the wife of Cotho Brackwood the current holder, and Nynelle Stenworth the one who held it immediately before. The Chapter 29 handoff to the wife of Halan Hollwood is the step just before this, so I am taking her to be Nynelle Stenworth. The record never names her.

Answer: Nynelle Stenworth

The bone chalice's chain of holders, in order:

- Tassa Brackwood kept it first.
- Tassa gave it to Red Jovus (Chapter 5).
- Rira won it at cards from the husband of Rira Stenworth (Chapter 21).
- Rira Stenworth pressed it into the hands of Red Jovus (Chapter 30).
- Red Jovus gave it to the wife of Jovus Brackwood (Chapter 33).

The latest transfer is the one in Chapter 33, so the current holder is the wife of Jovus Brackwood. The person who held it immediately before her is Red Jovus.
